title: The 2004 Microscope Study That Explained Water Striders
description:
A water strider never sinks. The old explanation was wax on its legs plus surface tension, the stretchy skin on top of water. In 2004, Xuefeng Gao and Lei Jiang at the Chinese Academy of Sciences put the legs under a microscope: they're covered in needle-shaped hairs under 3 micrometers wide (a human hair is 80-100), each carved with nano-scale grooves that trap air. The leg rides on a cushion of air, and a single leg held about 15 times the insect's body weight. Wax alone, on a fake leg, was enough to stand still but not to dart. To move, it rows its middle legs like oars, pushing swirls of water under the surface (MIT, 2003).
